correctness.rationale: The disease-free susceptible levels follow directly from the printed equations. The two-state next-generation matrix is reconstructed from the exact human and vector infection terms and removal rates, yielding characteristic polynomial z^2-a z-c. The earlier-model type threshold a+c has the same one-crossing because p(1)=1-a-c. Loss of immunity does not enter the infected subsystem, while human recovery and disease mortality enter only through the positive removal rate q_h, proving zero and negative sensitivities respectively. Exact rational arithmetic reproduces the full type-threshold sensitivity table, and high-precision eigenvalue and finite-difference checks replay the spectral calculation.

originality.rationale: Next-generation matrices, normalized sensitivities, and direct-plus-vector threshold decompositions are prior art and are not claimed as new. The accepted originality is the source-specific correction: the 2022 paper's Section 7 assigns positive sensitivity to parameters whose exact model sensitivities are zero or negative, and substantially misranks the direct and vector-mediated transmission elasticities at its own parameter set. Exact-source and alias searches found no published correction of these sensitivity conclusions.
residual_risks: The 2022 paper does not clearly display the algebraic reproduction-number formula it differentiated, so the report compares its stated sensitivity conclusions to both standard threshold conventions derived from the printed model.
A non-indexed author correction could exist outside the searched records.
The fractional Caputo-Fabrizio stability problem may have additional order-dependent spectral conditions; the accepted claim is restricted to the epidemiological invasion-threshold sensitivity.

value.rationale: Section 7 explicitly motivates sensitivity analysis as a guide to reducing infection spread and designing control strategies. The corrected calculation reverses the signs of recovery and disease-induced removal, makes loss of immunity exactly irrelevant to invasion, and shows that the vector-mediated route has three orders of magnitude less elasticity than the direct human route at the paper's own parameter set. This changes the biological interpretation and parameter prioritization rather than merely correcting a typographical coefficient.
